rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ. ⲡⲙⲟⲩ ⲉⲧⲟ ⲛⲣ̄ⲡⲟ = 'Death who is king/reigning.' Cf. ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'kingship' line 33.
Reduplicated verbal form related to ⲃⲗⲃⲗ / ϫⲱϩⲙ̄. Used of how the teaching of Error defiles human beings.
Greek loanword πανουργία. Stock pejorative term for Error's deceptive sophistication.
Greek loanword αἰχμαλωτίζω. Used of Error capturing the wise.
Standard Coptic ⲑⲃⲃⲓⲟ. Used of Error humbling the wise to its tree before casting them into eternal punishment. Maintains downward semantics paralleling ϩⲃⲱⲣⲃ ('cast down').
Lycopolitan compound ⲥⲟⲩⲛ̄ + ⲟⲩⲱⲛ — verb of recognition/identification used of recognizing the evil seeds within false doctrine.
Plural of agricultural-cosmological term, distinct from ⲡⲃⲣⲉ ('seed' singular). Here: 'evil seeds' = the corrupting principles within false doctrines.
ⲥⲛⲁϩ = 'bond, fetter, that-which-binds.' Here: 'their bond' — what binds the soul to its true nature, opposed to the alien seeds.
Greek loanword ταμιεῖον. Standard Manichaean term for the five primordial dark depositories from which the elements gushed forth. The five-fold cosmological inventory of darkness.
Standard Coptic verb of gushing/welling-up. Cosmogonic verb: the five elements gushed from the storehouses; the five storehouses themselves gushed from the land of darkness.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲕⲁⲕⲉ 'darkness.' Standard cosmological pole opposed to the Light. Capitalized when functioning as the cosmic principle.
Greek loanword στοιχεῖον. Technical Manichaean term for the five primordial elements (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) that gushed from the five storehouses.
Greek loanword πλάσσειν. Standard Manichaean verb for archonic fashioning — molding the five trees from the elements, then molding the five kinds of creatures from the trees.
Greek γένος + Coptic ⲥⲱⲛⲧ̄ ('creature'). The five archonic creature-kinds molded in each dark world, male and female.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲡⲉ 'taste, savor.' Fifth correspondence-register in the Manichaean cosmological mapping: each of the five dark bodies IS a taste. Direct correspondence — the body and the taste are one thing at different registers.
Greek loanword καπνός. The first of the five dark worlds in the Manichaean cosmological schema — ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ⲙⲡⲕⲁⲡⲛⲟⲥ = 'the world of smoke.' Cf. ⲕⲣⲙⲉⲥ (native Coptic 'smoke') in earlier vocab.
Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲓⲕ / ϣⲓⲕϩ 'depth, abyss.' Used of the dark depths from which the smoke-world arose. Parallel cosmological pole to ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲛ ('the Deep').
Lexeme unclear; translated interpretively from context as 'the wellspring of all evil and wickedness.' May derive from a root meaning 'pit, source, abyssal origin.' Confidence low.
Greek loanword κακία. Paired with ⲡⲟⲛⲏⲣⲓⲁ ('wickedness') as the totality of moral darkness.
Greek loanword πονηρία. Paired with ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ — the comprehensive negative quality of the dark realm.
Greek loanword πόλεμος. The first cosmic war originated through the smoke-world's stirring.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲙⲗⲁϩ 'strife, quarrel.' Listed among the conflicts originated from the dark world of smoke.
Standard Coptic ⲙⲓϣⲉ 'fight, battle.' Used in plural inventory of conflict-types.
Abstract from ⲧⲱⲛ 'rise up against.' Used in the inventory of conflict-types.
Greek loanword κίνδυνος. Listed among the war-conflicts of the dark cosmos.
Possibly a martial term for combat/struggle. Listed in the conflict-inventory.
Greek loanword πύλη. ⲡⲏⲗⲏ ⲛⲥⲱⲭⲉ = 'gates of slaughter/wounding.'
Tentative; lexeme unclear in this context. May relate to a root meaning 'strike, smite, wound.' Fits the martial inventory.
ⲭⲁⲥⲉ = 'high, lofty' (cf. ⲡⲭⲥⲉ in earlier vocab). The elevated dominion of the King of Darkness over the five dark worlds.

Standard Manichaean title for the supreme ruler of the dark realms — a five-formed cosmic adversary whose body parts correspond to lion, demons, eagle, dragon, fish (the latter implied by continuation onto next page).
Standard Coptic 'lion.' First of the five animal-correspondences for the body of the King of Darkness — his head IS a lion.
Greek loanword δαίμων. Second register of correspondence: hands/feet of the King of Darkness ARE demons.
Coptic ⲁϩⲱⲙ 'eagle.' Fourth (here third in surviving order) animal-correspondence: shoulders of the King of Darkness ARE eagles.
Greek loanword δράκων. Belly of the King of Darkness IS a dragon — restored from standard schema.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲱⲣⲉ/ϭⲓϫ 'hand.' Body-part in the five-form correspondence inventory of the King of Darkness.
Coptic ⲛⲁϩⲃ 'shoulder.' Body-part in the five-form correspondence series.
